before: He said to them: 'It is not for you to know the times or the seasons which the Father has set in his own authority' (Acts 1:7).

For it is not necessary to be overly curious about things that are too secret and hidden in God, and through these things he taught; rather, they wanted to go and were very youthful towards what is beneficial, and they wanted to fulfill the ministry of the apostleship, having entrusted the knowledge of all things to God.
And there appeared to them divided tongues like fire.
Some spoke with tongues, although they did not know them before; others understood, interpreting, although they had not previously been accustomed to such things.

The divine Paul boasts of those who then received the grace to speak in tongues, not as a portion of charisma, but as a sign in order to the faithful, and he also set forth a prophetic word: 'That I will speak in different tongues and different lips to this people, and even so they will not believe' (Isaiah 28:11).
The Spirit distributed the gifts of charisma in different ways.

Just as, he says, this thick body from the earth was composed of small particles, so also Christ—that is, his body, which is the Church—has a constitution that is most perfect in its spiritual unity through a great multitude of holy people.
And after a little while: when those who were mystagogues under the sun were about to proclaim the evangelical and saving message to every nation and every language, the tongues gave them a sign.

Being men of Galilee and having been brought up in Judea, Hebrews and from Hebrews, Medes and Parthians, and indeed Elamites, and those from the middle of the flowing rivers, Cappadocians and Egyptians, they spoke in their own languages; and the matter was being accomplished for them by the Spirit's working and grace.
For it is written that there appeared to them divided tongues like fire, and the following things.
But the manner of the economy was what was being done; however, not all understood.

Since they once spoke in other languages, they made a display of the grace done through the Spirit, receiving the sign as an occasion for boasting and an opportunity for greed; they were careless about discussing the things of the holy prophets and the evangelical doctrines with the crowds, as it had been proclaimed from above and from long ago.
They were revering the ability to speak in tongues as the only thing, and thought it necessary to be transformed only in this; and the matter was among the most urgent preoccupations.
'And I will give wonders in the heaven above, and signs on the earth below' (Matthew 24:29).

The holy Cyril says that the things that happened upon the cross of Christ are clearly taught, as are the things happening to the Jews through the Roman war; he says that the great and manifest day of Christ is the day of his resurrection: 'the sun will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood' (Matthew 24:29).

before: For a mind and understanding that are most perfect have a clear proof: they have nothing worthless on their tongue, and they endure not speaking foolishly. Instead, they consider it worthy of all speech to know how to speak well and say things full of all praise. For speaking wisdom is most necessary, especially for those who have chosen to live well. Holy people reject speaking foolishly, and it is unaccustomed for them to use jests or shameful talk, as the all-wise Paul says.

They love to speak well, for they remember the holy Scripture which says, 'Your speech should be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may give grace to those who hear' (Colossians 4:6). The scripture that is inspired by God accepts gentle speech, but rightly condemns the uncontrolled tongue (Titus 1:8). For it says, 'If someone does not stumble in speech, this one is a perfect man, able to control the whole body' (James 3:2). David sings, 'Set a guard, Lord, over my mouth, and a door of restraint over my lips' (Psalm 51:1). He also says, 'I will guard my ways, so that I do not sin with my tongue' (Psalm 34:13). The best guard is to have an untainted tongue. Do not speak against one another, brothers; for the one who speaks against a brother and judges his brother speaks against the law and judges the law (Romans 2:1). Every difficult passion of our thoughts puts away the beginning and birth of pride. Although it is necessary for some to examine themselves and live according to God, they do not do this, but rather meddle in the affairs of others.

When people see others who are weak, they often use this as an opportunity to slander and condemn them, as if they have forgotten about their own weaknesses. However, in doing so, they are actually condemning themselves, because they suffer from the same flaws as those they are criticizing. This is a point that even the wisest of writers, Paul, has made—that when we judge others, we are essentially condemning ourselves, since we are guilty of the same things.

There are those who are driven by a desire for wealth and gain, and they will endure all sorts of hardships, including long journeys and dangerous navigation, in pursuit of their goals. Others use their power and influence to exploit and take advantage of others, while some accumulate their wealth through unjust and wicked means, such as collecting excessive interest on loans. But to those who are rich and powerful, the warning is clear: your wealth will ultimately rot and decay, your fine clothes will be eaten away by moths, and your gold and silver will be corrupted. Weep and wail, for your troubles are coming.

before: The sandal of your feet is a sign of death and corruption, for every sandal is a remnant of a dead and corrupted animal, and thus Christ is inaccessible to those who are still bound by the law and pedagogical worship.

It is necessary to remove the stain and the dirt from sin, and to wipe away the dirt that comes from sin, which includes removing the filth that arises from sin, and also to remove the defilement and to scrape off the dirt that comes from sin, in order to be transplanted beyond Babylon.
You have filled up the evil of the Moabites, neighbor of Damascus, therefore you will be expelled from Damascus to Babylon.
Jacob asked to find a dwelling place for God, saying that he would not rest until he found the place of the Lord and the dwelling of God, which is clearly Christ (Genesis 28:22).
However, Solomon built a house for him, but the Most High does not dwell in handmade temples (1 Kings 8:27).

The wise Solomon built a famous temple in Jerusalem, and the crowd of Jews was very pleased with it, thinking that God had dwelled in it, but they were slow to understand and ignorant of the words of God.

They thought Jerusalem was the city of God and that he dwelled only in it, but God rebukes those who think small, saying, 'What kind of house will you build for me, who has the heaven as a throne and the earth as a footstool?' (Isaiah 66:1-2, Acts 7:49-50).
Stephen was stoned, calling out and saying, 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59).
As the holy Cyril says, I commit my spirit into your hands.
This is a great and extraordinary achievement for our souls, as Stephen, with his knees down, cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' (Luke 23:34, Acts 7:60).
After saying this, he fell asleep.
Saul was in agreement with his murder.

Stephen's prayer was not just a simple one, but one that was said with attention and care, as he was apologizing, saying that not even the previous things were of anger, he says, 'Lord', and wanting to draw them to this.
For just as he was apologizing, he was able to leave his anger and wrath behind, and cleanse his soul of the passion, making his words acceptable.

In the introductions of his preaching, Stephen was like a river flowing above the rest, silencing all his opponents and stopping the shameless tongues of the Jews, who were unable to withstand him, as he was confounding all the Jewish things, and setting up a bright trophy and a manifest victory.
He was a generous and wise man, full of grace, and his preaching benefited the Church greatly, even though he did not preach for a long time.
Unfortunately, he was suddenly seized and condemned as a blasphemer, and stoned.
